title: Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act
official_title: To amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) and passed the House by voice vote (no recorded roll call); the bill reauthorizes an existing utility-cybersecurity grant program and now awaits Senate consideration.
summary: Renews a federal program that helps rural, municipal, and small electric utilities defend their systems against cyberattacks. It gives the Secretary $250M over five years to hand out grants, technical assistance, and prizes to utilities that often lack their own cybersecurity resources.
brief: Reauthorizes the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program and authorizes $250M for it through 2030.

top_lines.headline: What the Utility Cybersecurity Program Does
subs: The Secretary awards grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes to eligible utilities
Deploys cybersecurity technology and expands threat information sharing
Provides technical assistance to protect, detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats

top_lines.headline: Who Is Eligible and Prioritized
subs: Covers rural co-ops, municipal utilities, and investor-owned utilities selling under 4,000,000 MWh/year
Includes not-for-profits partnered with at least 6 qualifying utilities
Priority for entities with limited cyber resources or bulk-power/defense-critical assets

top_lines.headline: Funding and Information Protection
subs: Authorizes $250M for the program for fiscal years 2026 through 2030
Information shared under the program is exempt from FOIA and state open-records laws
Awards may be made on a competitive or noncompetitive basis

items.main: Names the Act the "Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program

items.main: Amends Section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18723) to have the Secretary maintain the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program, providing technical assistance and funding to eligible electric utilities to protect against, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats.
items.detail: The Secretary awards funding through grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes on a competitive or noncompetitive basis, develops award criteria, and establishes a process to inform all eligible entities of opportunities. The program's objectives are to deploy advanced cybersecurity technologies for electric utility systems and to increase eligible entities' participation in cybersecurity threat information sharing programs.

items.main: Defines eligible entities as rural electric cooperatives, municipally owned or other political-subdivision utilities, not-for-profits partnered with at least 6 such utilities, and investor-owned utilities that sell less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours per year.
items.detail: In awarding funding and technical assistance, the Secretary must give priority to an eligible entity that has limited cybersecurity resources, owns assets critical to the reliability of the bulk-power system, or owns or operates defense critical electric infrastructure. The terms bulk-power system and defense critical electric infrastructure take their meanings from sections 215(a) and 215A(a) of the Federal Power Act.

items.main: Deems information shared by or with government under the program to be voluntarily shared and exempts it from the Freedom of Information Act and any state, Tribal, or local open-records, open-meetings, or sunshine law.
items.detail: Authorizes $250M to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out the section for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030. Awards and technical assistance are subject to the availability of appropriations.

underreported.summary: Information shared by or with the Federal Government or a State, Tribal, or local government under the program is deemed voluntarily shared and exempted from FOIA and from any state, Tribal, or local freedom-of-information, open-government, open-meetings, open-records, or sunshine law.
underreported.why_unreported: The section is titled and structured as a grant and technical-assistance program (subsections (b) through (d)), but subsection (e) also creates a broad disclosure exemption reaching state, Tribal, and local transparency laws, an effect not apparent from the program's funding-and-assistance label.

underreported.summary: Investor-owned electric utilities qualify as eligible entities if they sell less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year.
underreported.why_unreported: The program is titled for rural and municipal utilities, but the eligibility definition also extends to smaller investor-owned utilities meeting the sales threshold.

gaps: The bill authorizes $250M for the program but does not specify how the funds are allocated across fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
The program prioritizes entities that own defense critical electric infrastructure but does not set a minimum share of funding for that category.
The bill exempts shared information from disclosure laws but does not address how long that information is retained or when the exemption ends.
The program is directed at eligible entities with limited cybersecurity resources but sets no numeric threshold defining what counts as limited.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Miller-Meeks
featured_quotes.text: Just this spring, national security experts warned that hostile nation-states are shifting from isolated cyber incidents to sustained campaigns against U.S. critical infrastructure, including the energy sector. Yet, many small and rural utilities lack the capacity and expertise to act on this information. RMUC is designed to close that gap. In Iowa's First District, rural electric cooperatives serve ratepayers across 20 counties and face the same threats as major urban systems but with fewer resources.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. McClellan
featured_quotes.text: This bill represents the sort of bipartisan work that is important for the security and stability of the American grid and the safety of the American people. This bill reauthorizes the vital RMUC program, which helps rural and small municipalities to protect themselves against ever-multiplying and more sophisticated cybersecurity threats that could prove severely disruptive to small and rural communities alike, just like the ones I represent in Virginia's Fourth Congressional District.

added: Authorizes $250M for the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program for fiscal years 2026 through 2030
modified: Amends Section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18723) by replacing it with the reauthorized program text
